name: Kabardian
sources: Colarusso 1992, A Grammar of the Kabardian Language, §2.5.1, p. 16: stress "is confined to the last stem morpheme, and does not shift back to most affixes"; §2.5.2, p. 17: "final vowels cannot receive normal stress"

Kuipers 1960, Phoneme and Morpheme in Kabardian, §14, p. 35: "if prefixes are added to a monosyllable ending in ā the stress does not move back but remains on ā"; "the sequences Cī, Cē, Cū, Cō, Cā (where C stands for any consonant) have in common that they end in a long vowel"

Gordon & Applebaum 2010, Acoustic correlates of stress in Turkish and Kabardian, JIPA 40(1), §2.3, p. 37: stress falls on "the final syllable if it is heavy, i.e. contains either a long vowel (CVV) or a coda consonant (CVC), and the penult if the final syllable is light"
Kuipers 1960, Phoneme and Morpheme in Kabardian, appendix "Kabardian alphabets", pp. 116-118 (page image): э = /a/ (short), ы = /ə/, а = /ā/, о = /aw/, у = /əw/ or /w/, е = /aj/ or /ja/, я = /ja/
